correctness.rationale: For r<ell_min/3 each sampled interior point is within along-edge distance r of at most one endpoint. A ball of radius r cannot travel through a whole intervening edge. Away from endpoints it has length 2r; within distance t≤r of a degree-d endpoint its length is 2r+(d-2)(r-t), from the two directions on its own edge and the d-1 possible branches once it reaches the vertex. Integrating over the d edge ends at each vertex adds d(d-2)r²/2 to the unnormalized pair volume. This gives the displayed CDF after division by L², including r=0 by atomlessness. Right differentiation gives exactly the two inverse formulas. The handshake identity gives the Betti formula and degree-two subdivision changes neither degree sum expression nor L. In a tree, summing binom(d-1,2) over the vertices yields B+1, and degree at most three leaves just the degree-three count. The upper bound counts unordered incident edge pairs; if every pair meets, two edges meeting at v force all other edges to meet at v or form a triangle, impossible in a tree. Equality at the bottom is exactly the no-branch path case, including one edge. The proof establishes the finding on its stated class. Simplicity is a standing restriction here, not an independently established necessity; the proof does not need the limitations paragraph's stronger wording about essentiality.
